articleTitle: Visualization of 3D, scalar and vector, static and time varying fields using the ANSYS general purpose finite element program
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Visualisation of Three-Dimensional Fields
abstract: ANSYS is a general purpose finite element program which has been under continuous development since its first commercial release in 1970. It is a standalone package that includes complete pre-processing and post-processing together with a wide variety of solution types, including stress, thermal, electromagnetics, fluid flow and combinations of these as coupled analyses. As it has such a wide variety of solution types it has been necessary to develop a wide variety of graphical tools to visualize the results.

articleTitle: Visualization of three dimensional vector fields and functions
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Visualisation of Three-Dimensional Fields
abstract: This paper will examine the reasons why it is necessary to display vector fields in three dimensions, the representations that have been used to display them and the display devices that are available. It is assumed that the need to display the field is connected with the numerical simulation of a continuum field distribution, in particular with electromagnetic fields. A finite element solution contains a large amount of information that it would often be impossible to obtain by measurement, for example magnetic field and electric current distributions inside materials. This information can be of value to the designer of products and also to the developer of numerical methods.

articleTitle: Using VISUAL3 for three dimensional time domain unstructured electromagnetic visualisation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Visualisation of Three-Dimensional Fields
abstract: Summary form only. The visualisation of time domain electromagnetic calculations on unstructured meshes requires both high performance graphics workstations and high performance graphical software. We have made use of the public domain VISUAL3 software from MIT, which consists of a highly optimised environment (both in terms of memory requirements and computational efficiency) for 3D visualisation. Our primary use of VISUAL3 has been as a development tool giving accurate and fast visualisation of results obtained during development of the unstructured EM code. The ability to represent vectors in the 2D and 3D windows provides an simple way to check the polarisation; interactive selection and manipulation of these displays was essential to obtain uncluttered representations. The paper illustrates these capabilities by showing the visualisation of scattering from a 3D object.

articleTitle: Integrating sign language into a virtual reality environments
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Visualisation of Three-Dimensional Fields
abstract: In a multi-user distributed virtual reality environment, such as DIVE (Distributed Interactive Virtual Environment) where the various participants each have a 3-D representation, a model for interaction is necessary. The Spatial Interaction Model describes how objects should interact with each other in the virtual environment. This model has since been extended to cover more interactions and is described in the paper. Language and gesture can be coordinated to form a single communication system more powerful than either alone. Hand gesture in particular is critical for fast interactive human to human communication. A VR system that allows a sign language channel and thus also a gestural channel will have an enriched communication medium. The main concept of this paper is that in a virtual reality environment it is possible to support users with different capabilities for interaction. The factors considered are whether the user can hear or not; their ability to use sign language; and the technology they have at their disposal on entry into the VR environment. A user is thus represented in the virtual environment as an entity with those capabilities available to it.

articleTitle: Visualisation of scalar and vector fields with visual programme construction
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Visualisation of Three-Dimensional Fields
abstract: The software package "AVS/Express" provides tools for the visualization of complex scientific data however also allows researchers to create experimental data representations. Field data interpretation applications are constructed using a visual programming environment, and includes graphical user interface tools (GUI). AVS/Express presents a screen giving overall control of the operating paradigm. Called the "network editor", it contains iconic representations of programme modules. Coloured lines connecting the modules represent data and control relationships in the application. Unlike other programming environments, no distinction is made between library components and running versions of these components, and dynamic changes of the running programme is allowed. The modules in the network editor are managed by the system provided object manager. Control, messages, and shared data areas are managed by the object manager. The objects defined in the system, as well as the visual programming system and the object manager, are based on object oriented concepts. How the system behaves with regards to a traditional C++ program development environment is summarised.
